body.x: In logistics centers, shipyards and maintenance depots, much field work still relies on manual steps and the knowledge of a few experts. Picking errors, missed checklist items and delays in reaching the right drawing or manual follow from that.
What if a worker could look at a piece of equipment and see its drawings, manuals and checklist at the worksite, hands free?

DEEP.FINE Co., Ltd., a Seoul-based industrial operations platform company founded in 2019 and led by CEO Hyunbae Kim, builds that workflow with Vision AI, AI agents, a Visual Positioning System (VPS), AR and XR, and AI-glasses-based computing. At KES 2026, the company is showcasing two solutions, DAO and its Smart Logistics Solution, and plans to demonstrate realistic workflows for both.

DAO is a smart-glasses-based AI solution for field work instructions. Using Vision AI and optical character recognition (OCR), it recognizes equipment tags, QR codes and text in the worker's field of view and shows the related information on site. It also supports drawing and manual access, checklist execution, activity recording, report generation and remote collaboration with experts. The Smart Logistics Solution supports picking, verification and sorting with real-time information on products, quantities and locations. Barcode and QR verification compares actual work against work instructions to catch mismatches before shipment. Through smart glasses and tablets, it provides work guidance, tote mapping, AI-based verification and automatic collection of operational data, without major changes to existing logistics-center infrastructure.

The platform runs on-premises or as software-as-a-service (SaaS) through a hybrid architecture built for enterprise and industrial security requirements. DEEP.FINE has carried out digital transformation projects with major Korean enterprises and public-sector organizations in logistics, manufacturing, shipbuilding, heavy industry and maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO), and says some have moved from technical validation to actual operation and expansion. It is also leading a Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy R&D project on AI smart-glasses technology for logistics.

DEEP.FINE is preparing to take what it has built at Korean industrial sites to overseas markets with smart manufacturing, digital logistics and equipment maintenance in focus. It is looking for system integrators, industrial solution providers and technology partners who understand local operations and can support technical reviews, proof of concept (PoC) projects and deployment, rather than simple distributors.

Next, the company plans to turn project-based work into standardized solutions that can be deployed repeatedly, extending DAO across manufacturing, shipbuilding and MRO and widening its logistics offering to loading and unloading. It names differences in ERP, MES and WMS systems across industries and countries as a main challenge abroad, and says local PoC opportunities and industry-specific reference cases would help it enter new markets.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
